about.how.s1: A new round opens every Monday, and everyone who joins picks their free times for the week.
about.how.s2: Once enough people join, you get suggestions ranked by shared interests, goals and overlapping free time. You can also browse everyone by tags.
about.how.s3: Tap "I'd like to meet" on anyone. If they say yes too, it's a match; if they skip, nobody gets notified.
about.how.s4: After a match you both see each other's contact details and shared free times — tap one to lock it in, and tell us afterwards whether you met.

about.name.text: Yalelux = Yale + lux, Latin for "light" — from Yale's motto, Lux et Veritas (Light and Truth). We'd like it to work like a lamp: lighting up Yalies scattered around the world and bringing them together.

about.now.text: One round a week: fill in a profile, pick a few free times, and we'll suggest a few people you might click with — or browse by tags yourself. When you both tap "I'd like to meet", you swap contact details and grab a coffee, in person or online. Every so often there's a themed Coffee Chat week or month.
about.now.title: First up: Coffee Chat
about.privacy.ai.now.mineOff: Right now: smart ranking is enabled, but your switch is off, so none of your details are sent to DeepSeek.
about.privacy.ai.now.mineOn: Right now: smart ranking is enabled, and your switch is on.
about.privacy.ai.now.off: Right now: smart ranking isn't enabled, so nothing is sent to DeepSeek.
about.privacy.ai.now.on: Right now: smart ranking is enabled and on by default for new accounts.
about.privacy.ai.p1: The site and its database run on a server in the United States. If you use Yalelux from mainland China, your information is transferred abroad.
about.privacy.ai.p2: Smart ranking is on by default whenever we've enabled the service. While it's on, we send anonymised details — student or alum, stage, class year, questionnaire answers and your one-line intro, under a temporary ID — to DeepSeek, a company in China, to help order suggestions. While your switch is on, your anonymised details may also be sent as a candidate when someone else's suggestions are ranked. Your name, emails, contact handle, job and city are never sent.
about.privacy.ai.p3: If you'd rather not take part, switch it off under "Me" anytime. You'll then get rule-based suggestions only (shared interests, goals and free times), and your details are no longer sent to DeepSeek. If you don't see the switch under "Me", the service isn't enabled right now and nothing is sent. Your intro is free text, so please keep contact details and your full name out of it.
about.privacy.ai.title: Smart ranking and cross-border data

about.privacy.contact.text: Questions about privacy, or want to see or delete specific data? Sign in and leave a note in the feedback box — an ACSSY volunteer will follow up.
about.privacy.contact.title: Contact us
about.privacy.delete.keep: We keep your profile and records for as long as your account exists, so you can pick up each week. There's no automatic expiry yet — the one exception is sign-in codes and the network address recorded when you request one, which are cleared a day after they expire. Once retention periods are set, they'll be listed here and the version number will go up.
about.privacy.delete.left.audit: Your user ID and the actions you took, in the activity log (no name or email), for security audits.
about.privacy.delete.left.backup: The database is backed up daily and the last 30 backups are kept, so your data can stay in backups for up to 30 days after deletion.
about.privacy.delete.left.firstCode: The record of the sign-in code email sent before your account existed (including the Yale address it went to).
about.privacy.delete.left.recs: Your user ID may remain in other people's suggestion records.
about.privacy.delete.left.sent: Emails already delivered to other people's inboxes can't be recalled.
about.privacy.delete.p1: You can delete your account under "Me" anytime. Deletion is immediate and removes your profile, contact email and contact handle, settings and consent record, your free times in every round, all invites and matches you sent or received (including notes), your suggestion records, sign-in sessions, codes and the network addresses recorded with them, the log of emails sent to you, and anything you wrote in the feedback box.
about.privacy.delete.title: Keeping and deleting

about.privacy.email.title: Emails
about.privacy.email.unsub: Every optional email has an unsubscribe link at the bottom: open it and tap "Unsubscribe" to confirm — no sign-in needed. You can also switch each type on or off under "Me" anytime. Emails go out through a delivery service (such as Resend, in the US), which handles your address and the message content.

about.privacy.intro: In plain words: what Yalelux collects, who can see it, where it's stored, and how you stay in control.
about.privacy.security.audit: Every change — sign-ins, profile edits, invites, replies, scheduling, publishing events, account deletion — is recorded in an audit log.
about.privacy.security.cookie: Your sign-in token lives only in an httpOnly cookie that page scripts can't read. The server stores just a hash of it, so even a leaked database can't be used to sign in.
about.privacy.security.secrets: Secrets live only in the server's environment, never in the code repository.
about.privacy.security.title: Security
about.privacy.see.admin.what: ACSSY volunteers. They see aggregate numbers, the feedback box (with submitters' names), the email log (without addresses) and the activity log (user IDs only) — never your contact handle, emails, detailed answers or invite notes.
about.privacy.see.intro: You can always see all of your own data. Everyone else:
about.privacy.see.invited.what: All of the above, plus your note.
about.privacy.see.mutual.what: All of the above, plus your contact handle (e.g. WeChat) and the time you agree on.
about.privacy.see.nobody.what: Your sign-in codes, who you skipped, and your email addresses — no other user or admin can see these.
about.privacy.see.others.what: Your name, a one-line identity (for students, stage and class year, e.g. "Master's · Class of 2027"; for alumni, job and city), your public questionnaire answers, and the free times you share.
about.privacy.see.server.what: Can technically access the whole database, so server access is limited to one or two people.
about.privacy.see.title: Who can see what
about.privacy.summary: We collect only what coffee matching needs; your contact details go only to people you've both said yes to; smart ranking (on by default) and most emails can be switched off, and you can delete your account anytime.
about.privacy.title: How we handle your information
